body:
SLICE TWO, USING YOUR METHOD RATHER THAN A PATTERN - AND IT FOUND A SECOND HOLE, IN THE SAME MODULE,
REACHABLE FROM THE WIRE WITH NO VALIDATION AT ALL.

I applied your filter: numeric-parameter enum cases, then READ them. 67 candidates, and the
classification does most of the work:

  37 are in ERROR/DIAGNOSTIC enums - ChartViolation, PenmanError, PatchError, DomainError,
     EmbedError and friends. Their Ints are offsets and indices being REPORTED. There is no lawful
     subrange for "the offset where parsing failed", so none of them is invariant-bearing.
  30 are in VALUE/CONFIG enums across 15 types. That is the readable set.

Your KernelShape.Rectangular(bandwidth) came out of that filter independently, which is how I know
the filter works rather than merely agrees with me.

THE NEW ONE: MissingValuePolicy.RequireMinCoverage(fraction: Double), features/derivation.scala:29.

  DECODED FROM THE WIRE WITH NO CHECK -
    codec/features.scala:333  field[Double](c, "fraction").map(MissingValuePolicy.RequireMinCoverage.apply)
  No guard anywhere - six references in main, none validating.

  THE CONSUMER, features/window.scala:384 -
    case MissingValuePolicy.RequireMinCoverage(f) if cov.fraction < f => Missing(Excluded)
    case _                                                            => reducer.reduce(nev)

  MEASURED, not reasoned:
    cov=0.10 f=0.90   EXCLUDED     <- normal: under-covered, withheld
    cov=0.10 f=NaN    PUBLISHED
    cov=0.00 f=NaN    PUBLISHED    <- ZERO coverage, published
    cov=0.10 f=-1.0   PUBLISHED
    cov=0.99 f=5.0    EXCLUDED

A NaN or negative minimum-coverage threshold means THE COVERAGE GATE NEVER EXCLUDES ANYTHING. The
policy whose entire purpose is withholding under-covered derivations silently withholds nothing, and
a value derived from ZERO observed samples is published as though measured. That is AGENTS rule 7's
polarity case exactly - `x < NaN` is false, so a bare comparison FAILS OPEN - and it is the same
shape as your bandwidth hole one line of the same module over.

WORSE THAN THE BANDWIDTH ONE IN ONE RESPECT, and I want to be careful not to overstate the rest: you
found no code constructing a NaN bandwidth, so that is a reachable hole with no producer. THIS ONE
HAS A PRODUCER - the decoder builds it from untrusted JSON with no validation. I have NOT found a
stored artifact containing such a value, so it remains a reachable hole rather than an observed
failure, but the reach is shorter.

NOT AN INCIDENT, AND NOT MINE TO FIX: features owns it, same as the bandwidth. The two want the same
remedy and should probably be one candidate - the wire boundary already exists in
codec/features.scala and both are one guard each. I have not touched anything; the probe above is a
scratch file and is not committed. Recording on bd-01M19NYZT593MXWEERP80RHY8J.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I read the 30 value/config cases well enough to rank them, not exhaustively. The
ones I judged plausible and did NOT chase are FeatureValueSchema.Vector(dimension),
TruncationPolicy.KeepHead(maxTokens) and LeakageVerdict.Clear(threshold). ThreadPolicy.All(max:
PositiveInt) is delegated and safe. Somebody should read those four rather than trust my ranking.
